newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees 7-plus pct growth for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees 7-plus pct growth for 1997.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Sunday predicted the Philippine gross national product growth to exceed seven percent this year from last year's 6.8 percent on the back of rising exports.

He said he expected the economy to sustain its growth into the year 2000 with GNP forecast to grow in the range of from nine to 10 percent by year 2002 and exports and investments expanding by 20 percent annually until then.

"We are now at 19 percent during the first two months of 1997 in terms of exports," he said, giving no comparative figures. He spoke at the graduation of cadets of the Philippine Military Academy in Baguio city in the northern Philippines.

Ramos said the reform programmes he launched when he took office in 1992 had helped cut down wealth disparities as the number of families living below the poverty threshhold fell to 35 percent last year from 40 percent five years ago.

"If these past five years have taught us anything about economics it is that nothing works better than a free market, but this also means that we must strive to keep the market free and accessible to all," he added.
